title: The Grace of Kings
author: Ken Liu
review:
I absolutely loved every minute of this book. Ken Liu has the potential to be one of my favorite writers. I have major respect for authors with a strong vision of what they want their story and narrative to be even if it's a little outside of normal conventions and sticking with it without any compromises.

This is definitely a dense and challenging read and demands that you pay attention to get the full experience, often Liu will not re-introduce characters even though there are a lot of them, and you often get a short flashback that fleshes out their backstory after being introduced to them. I'm in love with his writing style and he gets me to care about new characters faster than pretty much any author I've read before.

Liu's prose is top notch, I'm a self-admitted prose snob and there's no faster way to get me to quit a book than poor writing. Grace of Kings has gorgeous sections that relate humanity to nature, have deep introspective looks into family, nobility, philosophy and they're all interweaved flawlessly.

I'm also a theme-driven reader and the themes Liu explores in this book are tremendous, there's a ton of subtext in the book which rewards an attentive read. I was thinking of listening to this on audio but I'd highly recommend against that, there's a lot of section breaks and pauses that only really come across well in the physical text.

This felt like a whole trilogy or series in a single book, a lot happens and the third person omniscient perspective really helps move things along, I can see this being contentious, but I personally love the risk Liu takes with this perspective since it's not common. It allows Liu to jump around and give the important events in the plot without restrictions.

Highly recommend this book, it's among the best I've read. Can't wait to continue the series, it's been the most excited I've been about an author's work in quite some time.
